footer.topicText: This quiz is a photo-based nostalgia challenge about older gadgets, media formats, school tools, office items, and everyday analog objects.
footer.aboutText: This photo quiz is a quick nostalgia challenge about older gadgets, media formats, school supplies, office tools, and everyday analog objects. It is made for entertainment and general trivia, not as a formal history guide. Item names, designs, and common uses can vary by region, era, and household, so each image is meant as a playful recognition clue.

stageGroups.title: Portable Tech
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice start. The next round moves from pocket gadgets into living-room classics.

questions.prompt: Before smartphones, people carried this device to receive short numeric messages. What is it?
questions.explanation: Pagers were the height of mobile tech in the 90s; you'd get a beep and then have to find a payphone to call back!

questions.prompt: What was the primary purpose of a pencil when used with a cassette tape like this?
choices: To manually rewind or fix tangled tape
To stop the tape from playing
questions.explanation: If the tape got "eaten" by the player or needed rewinding to save battery, a hexagonal pencil fit perfectly into the gears.

questions.prompt: What are these "Rabbit Ears" found on top of old television sets used for?
questions.explanation: Before cable and satellite, you had to manually adjust these metal rods to get a clear picture (and sometimes add aluminum foil for better signal!).

questions.prompt: In the era of film photography, why was a "Red Light" used in a darkroom?
choices: To make the room look cool
To signal that the door is locked
To develop photos without exposing light-sensitive paper
questions.explanation: Photographic paper is less sensitive to red light, allowing photographers to see what they were doing without ruining the images during development.

questions.prompt: How did you "dial" a number on this type of vintage telephone?
choices: By rotating the finger wheel for each digit
By sliding a lever up and down
questions.explanation: On a rotary phone, you had to put your finger in the hole for each number and rotate the dial all the way to the metal finger stop.

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of this small plastic "Floppy Disk" before USB drives existed?
choices: To store and transfer digital files
questions.explanation: A standard 3.5-inch floppy disk could only hold 1.44 MB of data—barely enough for one high-quality photo today!

stageGroups.title: Home Entertainment
stageGroups.encouragement: Good memory lane work. Now the quiz shifts toward cameras, film, and photo clues.

questions.prompt: What did you have to do to a "Disposable Camera" after taking all the photos?
choices: Turn the whole camera in to a shop for developing
Press a "Print" button on the back
questions.explanation: These were single-use cameras; you gave the entire plastic body to a lab to get your physical prints.

questions.prompt: Before Google Maps, what did people keep in their car's glove box to find their way?
questions.explanation: Drivers had to pull over and unfold giant paper maps to figure out their route.

questions.prompt: What was this "Overhead Projector" used for in classrooms?
choices: Shining light through transparent sheets onto a wall
questions.explanation: Teachers wrote on clear plastic sheets (transparencies), and the machine projected their notes onto a large screen.

questions.prompt: What is this device that allowed people to listen to music on the go using "Cassette Tapes"?
questions.explanation: The Walkman revolutionized music by making it portable for the first time in 1979.

questions.prompt: What do you call this machine used for writing before computers became common?
questions.explanation: Every letter was physically stamped onto paper through an ink ribbon; there was no "Delete" key!

questions.prompt: What are these "Negative" strips found in old photo envelopes?
choices: Developed film used to make more prints
questions.explanation: Negatives were the original captured images; you needed them if you wanted to make extra copies of your photos.

stageGroups.title: Photography And Film
stageGroups.encouragement: You are keeping pace. The next items come from desks, classrooms, and offices.

questions.prompt: How did you change the channel on a very old TV without a remote?
choices: By turning a physical knob on the TV set
questions.explanation: Early TVs had "clunk" knobs that you had to manually click through channels 2 to 13.

questions.prompt: What was this "Phone Booth" used for on street corners?
choices: Making calls with coins or a card
questions.explanation: Before cell phones, you had to find a public payphone if you needed to call someone while out.

questions.prompt: What are these "Film Canisters" used to store?
questions.explanation: These light-proof plastic containers protected the film from being ruined by sunlight before use.

questions.prompt: What was a "VCR" machine used for in the living room?
questions.explanation: VCRs allowed families to watch movies at home or record TV shows to watch later.

questions.prompt: What is this "Slide Projector" tray used for?
questions.explanation: Families would gather around to watch "slide shows" of their vacations projected onto a white wall.

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the "Rewind" button on a VHS player?
choices: To move the tape back to the beginning after watching
questions.explanation: You had to rewind the physical tape to the start before you could watch it again (or return it to the rental store!).

stageGroups.title: School And Office Relics
stageGroups.encouragement: Strong run so far. The final round is full of everyday tools from the analog era.

questions.prompt: Before the internet, how did people look up a stranger's phone number?
choices: Using the "Yellow Pages" or "White Pages" (Phone Books)
questions.explanation: Massive thick books listed every household and business phone number in the city.

questions.prompt: What is this "Discman" used for?
questions.explanation: It was the successor to the Walkman, but if you bumped it while walking, the music would "skip."

questions.prompt: What was this "Manual Pencil Sharpener" (found in schools) famous for?
choices: Being mounted to the wall and turned with a crank
questions.explanation: Students would stand by the wall and turn the handle to sharpen their wooden pencils.

questions.prompt: What is this "Game Boy" famous for?
choices: Being the first handheld video game console with cartridges
questions.explanation: Released by Nintendo in 1989, it featured a monochrome green screen and "Tetris."

questions.prompt: What was the "Encyclopaedia Britannica" set used for?
questions.explanation: A full set of over 30 books contained the sum of human knowledge at the time.

questions.prompt: What do you call this device used to listen to large "Vinyl Records"?
questions.explanation: Records were the primary way to listen to albums at home before tapes and CDs.

questions.prompt: What was this "Fax Machine" used to send over phone lines?
questions.explanation: It "scanned" a paper at one end and printed a copy at the receiver's end almost instantly.

questions.prompt: What is this "Library Card Catalog" cabinet used for?
choices: Finding where a book is located in the library
questions.explanation: Every book had a physical card; you had to look through these wooden drawers to find the "call number."

questions.prompt: What did people use to listen to the radio before digital tuning?
questions.explanation: You had to carefully turn a knob to find the exact frequency for your favorite station.

questions.prompt: What was this "Carbon Paper" used for when typing or writing?
questions.explanation: Placing this blue/black paper between two sheets allowed you to "copy" what you wrote onto the bottom page.

questions.prompt: What was this "Film Projector" used for in a cinema?
choices: Playing 35mm film reels onto a screen
questions.explanation: Real film was threaded through the machine, which used a bright lamp to show the movie.

questions.prompt: What is this "Rolodex" used for on a desk?
choices: Storing business contacts and phone numbers
questions.explanation: It was a rotating file of small cards where people kept names and addresses.
